summary_paragraph: A woman with type 1 diabetes, anxiety, and gastroparesis was admitted for diabetic ketoacidosis triggered by insulin nonadherence amid worsening nausea and vomiting. She presented with severe hyperglycemia, dehydration, and abdominal discomfort. Treated initially in the MICU with an insulin drip and IV fluids, she had transient improvement but required re-initiation of the drip due to recurrent DKA. Her nausea resolved as her metabolic state stabilized, and she transitioned to subcutaneous insulin. Thiamine deficiency was identified and treated. Glargine was titrated but reduced due to fasting hypoglycemia. Anxiety was addressed with increased sertraline and continued lorazepam. Chronic back pain was managed with non-opioid therapies. She was discharged home with medication adjustments, including increased sertraline, thiamine supplementation, lidocaine patches, and a revised insulin regimen, along with follow-up plans for endocrinology, psychiatry, and GI.
